title: ASTRA 2026: 90-Point Security Attack Test Lab Audit Report

attacks.name: Patient-data tampering
attacks.explanation: SHA-256 digest recalculation detects modified clinical medication dose

attacks.name: Digital-signature forgery
attacks.explanation: Ed25519 signature generated with rogue key fails verification against trusted hospital public key

attacks.name: QR-code tampering
attacks.explanation: Offline verifier recomputes canonical digest and Ed25519 signature; rejects modified allergy

attacks.name: Fake QR generation
attacks.explanation: Entirely fake card signed with rogue key is rejected by trusted hospital verification key
attacks.mitigation: Pinning trusted public key on verifier (implemented)

attacks.name: Public-key substitution
attacks.explanation: Verifier strictly verifies against caller-supplied trusted public key, ignoring rogue keys
attacks.mitigation: QR never defines its own trust root (implemented)

attacks.name: Private-key theft simulation
attacks.expected: Cryptographically valid but subject to key revocation
attacks.actual: Architecture isolates keyId for revocation tracking
attacks.explanation: If the legitimate private key is stolen, generated signatures are mathematically valid until revoked
attacks.mitigation: Hardware Security Module (HSM) + automated KMS key revocation lists

attacks.name: Unauthorized signing
attacks.explanation: Standalone crypto library blocks signing without private key; future backend must enforce RBAC on /api/sign
attacks.mitigation: Backend Express JWT/RBAC middleware for doctor role

attacks.name: Fail-open verification
attacks.actual: All malformed inputs fail closed with valid: false
attacks.explanation: All verifiers default to false and safely catch all parsing/structural anomalies

attacks.name: Ransomware / EHR outage
attacks.explanation: Zero-network local cryptographic verification functions with zero backend/database dependencies

attacks.name: Patient identity substitution
attacks.explanation: Digital signature explicitly binds patientId; altering identifier breaks signature

attacks.name: Trust-root manipulation
attacks.explanation: Attacker-controlled issuer/signature cannot satisfy trusted public key verification

attacks.name: Security-critical field manipulation
attacks.actual: All 5 clinical fields individually cause verification failure
attacks.explanation: All critical clinical attributes are bound into the canonical signed payload

attacks.name: Replay attack
attacks.explanation: Timestamp binding allows verifier to enforce maxAge freshness window policy
attacks.mitigation: Timestamp binding and maxAge freshness verification (implemented)

attacks.name: Stale-card attack
attacks.explanation: Card expiration timestamp is checked against current time; expired cards fail verification

attacks.name: Version rollback
attacks.explanation: Version numbers in provenance header detect sequence rollback anomalies

attacks.name: Timestamp manipulation
attacks.explanation: IssuedAt timestamp is directly signed in the statement; altering timestamp breaks signature

attacks.name: Provenance forgery
attacks.explanation: Origin source ID is cryptographically bound in the signed statement

attacks.name: Source spoofing
attacks.explanation: Claiming a trusted hospital name with an untrusted private key fails signature verification

attacks.name: Man-in-the-middle simulation
attacks.explanation: In-transit modifications break SHA-256 integrity digest immediately

attacks.name: Signature stripping
attacks.explanation: Missing signature field triggers immediate fail-closed rejection

attacks.name: Partial-field tampering
attacks.explanation: Single-character change completely changes hash and fails digital signature verification
attacks.mitigation: Avalanche effect of SHA-256 and Ed25519 (implemented)

attacks.name: Malformed QR/payload attack
attacks.actual: All malformed inputs safely rejected with valid: false
attacks.explanation: Defensive try/catch boundaries prevent unhandled crashes on malformed inputs

attacks.name: Algorithm confusion attack
attacks.explanation: System enforces strict Ed25519 and SHA-256 algorithms; rejects algorithm downgrade

attacks.name: JSON canonicalization attack
attacks.explanation: RFC 8785 deterministic canonicalizer eliminates key ordering discrepancies

attacks.name: Unknown key attack
attacks.explanation: Signatures signed with unknown keys fail verification against trusted hospital keys

attacks.name: QR privacy

attacks.name: Unauthorized QR scanning

attacks.name: Offline verifier modification

attacks.name: Compromised device
attacks.expected: Data integrity holds, device integrity lost
attacks.explanation: Cryptographic verification assumes verifying runtime is untampered

attacks.name: Offline cache manipulation

attacks.name: Private key in Git audit
